articles.title: Scrooge screening with live orchestra comes to Heywood Civic
articles.excerpt: The 1951 film starring Alastair Sim will be shown with a live score from the three-piece FB Pocket Orchestra on Saturday 14 November.
articles.content_html:
A screening of the classic film Scrooge with a live three-piece orchestra is coming to Heywood Civic on Saturday 14 November.

The event starts at 8pm and pairs the 1951 film starring Alastair Sim with music performed by the FB Pocket Orchestra. The production is touring in the film’s 75th anniversary year.

The venue lists a running time of 90 minutes. Its Pay What You Can prices are £8.40 at the lower rate, £10.50 standard and £12.60 at the higher rate, all including the booking fee.

Rather than a stage adaptation, this is a showing of the film with live musical accompaniment. It follows Ebenezer Scrooge’s encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Future in the familiar Charles Dickens story.

The organisers say the music is based on Richard Addinsell’s original score. Heywood Civic’s listing explains that Paul Stevenson reconstructed the score by listening to and transcribing the film soundtrack, creating an arrangement for the ensemble.

The film has a U certificate. For local families and cinema fans, the event offers a chance to hear live musicians accompany a black-and-white Christmas classic at a borough venue.

Heywood Civic is on LCpl Stephen Shaw MC Way, Heywood, OL10 1LW. Tickets and the venue’s pricing information are available at https://heywoodcivic.co.uk/event/scrooge-u-live-to-film/. Check availability and the venue’s accessibility information before booking.

The event was announced in a press release supplied by FB Music and Media, with the date, running time and ticket prices checked against Heywood Civic’s listing on 28 October 2026.

articles.title: Rochdale council deputy leader detained briefly in Pakistan during civic visit
articles.excerpt: Councillor Daalat Ali was held for a short time upon arrival in Pakistan as part of a delegation aimed at strengthening ties with Sahiwal.
articles.content_html:
Councillor Daalat Ali, the deputy leader of Rochdale council, was detained by authorities for a short period upon his arrival in Pakistan. This incident occurred during a civic delegation visit to the city of Sahiwal, which is twinned with Rochdale. The delegation includes Rochdale's ceremonial mayor, Councillor Faisal Rana, and aims to strengthen relationships between the two areas, which have historical ties dating back to their twinning in 1998.

The council confirmed that the detention was brief and related to Councillor Ali's long-standing personal campaigning regarding the Kashmir region. A spokesperson for the council stated that such detentions are not uncommon for individuals travelling to this region, particularly those with political views. Fortunately, Councillor Ali is reported to be safe and well, having continued his travels and meetings with local officials after the incident.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office also acknowledged the situation, confirming that they were in contact with local authorities regarding the matter. While the exact reasons for Councillor Ali's detention have not been officially confirmed by Pakistani authorities, the council's statement reassured that he was able to resume his duties as part of the delegation shortly thereafter.

This visit is significant for Rochdale, as many residents have familial connections to Sahiwal. The delegation's activities include attending various events, such as the opening of a Sewing Machine Centre by the Al-Mahmood Foundation, which is part of the ongoing efforts to foster community ties and support local initiatives in both regions.

articles.title: Rochdale’s Deckers Hospitality Group acquires historic drinks wholesaler Tate-Smith
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale-based family group has bought the Malton drinks wholesaler, with existing staff staying and Harry Tate-Smith continuing as trading director.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale-based Deckers Hospitality Group has acquired North Yorkshire drinks wholesaler Tate-Smith, adding a business founded in 1888 to its portfolio.

The deal brings together two family businesses. Deckers is led by siblings Max Brierley and Victoria Cosgrove and operates in hospitality, wholesale and e-commerce.

Tate-Smith, based in Malton, supplies soft and alcoholic drinks across North Yorkshire. The business had been owned by the same family for six generations.

According to the announcement issued on 22 October, it will continue trading as Tate-Smith Ltd. All current staff will remain, and Harry Tate-Smith will continue in the business as trading director.

Paul and Cate Tate-Smith sold the company. Paul said the time was right to pass it to a business that could support its next stage, while retaining a role for their son.

Maxwell Brierley, of Deckers Hospitality Group, said: “Like us Tate-Smith is a family-run business with an impressive history. We felt it was the perfect fit for us as we continue to develop and grow our portfolio, and we welcome them to our family.”

For Rochdale, the acquisition marks an expansion of a locally based group into an established Yorkshire wholesale business. The release does not disclose a purchase price or announce any additional Rochdale jobs.

AAB and Schofield Sweeney advised Tate-Smith’s shareholders. Deckers was advised by Pannone Corporate and Cowgills, part of the Sumer Group.

articles.title: Heywood lollipop man forced to leap out of way as drivers ignore crossing
articles.excerpt: A car and a moped have been seized after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man in Heywood, forcing him to jump aside for safety.
articles.content_html:
A car and a moped have been seized by Greater Manchester Police after their drivers ignored a lollipop man in Heywood, forcing him to leap out of the way on two separate occasions. The incidents occurred on Bury Old Road on 13 and 14 October, as reported by Rochdale Borough Council.

Barry Jones, the lollipop man involved, was standing in the road when both vehicles failed to stop. The council noted that there have been 137 reported incidents of drivers not stopping for school crossing patrols across the borough in the last five years, highlighting a concerning trend regarding road safety near schools.

Following the incidents, police gathered evidence, including witness statements, which led to the seizure of the silver Skoda car and the moped. A recent change in law, effective from June, allows police to seize vehicles without issuing a warning first under the Police Reform Act 2002.

Dylan Williams, the cabinet member for highways, expressed gratitude to the police for their prompt action and stated that the council would continue to report such incidents and pursue prosecutions where possible. This situation underscores the importance of road safety, particularly in school zones, and the need for drivers to adhere to traffic regulations.

Seventeen arrests were made during a police operation targeting an organised crime group linked to violence in Heywood earlier this year.

Seventeen people have been arrested as police tackle an organised crime group in Rochdale and Heywood. This operation, named Operation Rivercrest, involved 250 officers executing a series of raids across multiple locations, including Rochdale, Heywood, Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside, and Yorkshire.

The arrests, which took place on the morning of October 27, 2026, included sixteen men aged between 19 and 49, who are suspected of various offences such as drug supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery. A 21-year-old woman was also arrested on suspicion of being involved in drug supply.

Detective Sergeant Hannah Taala from Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division stated that the operation was initiated following a violent incident in Heywood earlier this year, which resulted in serious injuries and the use of weapons, including machetes. A cannabis farm was discovered during the raids, further highlighting the extent of the criminal activities.

The police's focus on this crime group aims to disrupt their operations and enhance community safety. The investigation is ongoing, and further updates are expected as the police continue to address the issues surrounding organised crime in the area.

This morning, 250 officers carried out a series of raids as part of Operation Rivercrest which is targeting an organised crime group. Those arrested range in age from 19 to 49. Sixteen men have been arrested on suspicion of various offences, including drugs supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery. One woman, aged 21, was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of drugs. DS Hannah Taala, of Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division, said officers focused on the crime group after violence in Heywood earlier in the year . She said: “There was a large disorder in April, where multiple people were involved in violence in the Heywood area. “It ended in some quiet serious injuries, assaults, a stab wound, using vehicles in that disorder, weapons, machetes. A cannabis farm was discovered during the raids. Image: GMP “Op Rivercrest followed because we realised the risk that they posed the community. “When we identified who was responsible, we executed warrants and we retrieved a number of mobile phones. The evidence on the mobile phones was massive and uncovered a spider web of criminality.” DS Taala said the large-scale investigation uncovered a variety of offences that led to the co-ordinated operation today. She said: “Quite a lot of the offences that we’ve been investigating have been violent offences and drug offences within the community. “We struggle to get people to speak to us sometimes. People are frightened, people don’t want to provide statements when they’ve witnessed something. “We understand that they don’t want to do that and they don’t want to get involved, but we’re always there to listen, to speak to them if they’ve got any concerns.” DS Taala said the exploitation of vulnerable by organised crime gangs was a particular issue police are keen to tackle. It doesn’t stop here. “Every step of an investigation opens up another can of worms, and we keep going, and we keep going. “But at the minute, we’re focussing on what’s happening within our division of Rochdale.” DS Taala also appealed to people who have become caught up in an organised crime gang. “I have an issue with people taking advantage of vulnerable people, especially. “People need to understand the never in too deep. It doesn’t matter if they think we’re going to judge them, or if they think they’re going to get in trouble. “We’re always here, and willing to listen, not just to the people that are being exploited, but also to people that are concerned about them.” Warrants were executed this morning. articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a contract to MASSEY & HARRIS (ENGINEERING) LIMITED for the Queen's Park SEND and Improvement Project. This initiative aims to create a more inclusive play area at Queen's Park in Heywood, enhancing facilities for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND).

The project will involve several key improvements, including the extension of the existing play area, the installation of a dance arch, the creation of a sensory area surrounding the dance arch, and the addition of a wheelchair swing. These enhancements are designed to ensure that all children can enjoy the park's facilities, regardless of their physical abilities.

The decision to improve the play area reflects the council's commitment to inclusivity and accessibility in public spaces. By investing in these facilities, Rochdale Council aims to provide a safe and engaging environment for all children in the community, promoting social interaction and play.

The next steps will involve the commencement of construction works, with further updates expected as the project progresses. This development is significant for local families, particularly those with children who have SEND, as it will provide them with improved recreational opportunities in their community.

articles.title: Does a boggart still haunt Clegg Hall?
articles.excerpt: The house on Clegg Hall Road is real and protected, the boggart story is old — but the medieval “tragedy” that feeds the legend is not supported by contemporary records.
articles.summary: The house on Clegg Hall Road is real and protected, the boggart story is old — but the medieval “tragedy” that feeds the legend is not supported by contemporary records.
articles.body:
Short answer: there is no documentary proof that Clegg Hall was the scene of a medieval massacre and therefore no factual basis to claim a still‑active, historically verified haunting. The house that people call Clegg Hall survives as a recognisable historic building and the boggart tale survives as folklore recorded by Victorian collectors; the two things sit side by side, not one inside the other. ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

What we can say with confidence about place and period is plainly written in the records. The standing house on Clegg Hall Road is Grade II* on the National Heritage List for England and is described there as a house of about 1610, probably built for Theophilus Ashton; the list entry records its form, materials and a National Grid Reference (SD 92242 14490). The List entry is concerned with architecture and history, not ghost stories. ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

The boggart story — the thing people mean when they talk about “Clegg Hall” in the way they might say “that place is haunted” — is a well‑attested piece of Lancashire folklore. It was written down and popularised in the nineteenth century by folklorists and local balladists. John Roby included an extended narrative about the “Clegg‑Hall Boggart” in his Traditions of Lancashire, and nineteenth‑century collectors and compilers (and later commentators) preserved variants that add striking motifs: murdered heirs, demons walking the house, an exorcist who bargains for “a body and a soul” and then produces “the body of a cock and the sole of a shoe” as a trick to lay the spirits. Those details recur across Roby, local ballads and later folklore anthologies. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25256/25256-h/25256-h.htm))

That still leaves a gap between colourful tale and verifiable fact. County historians who examined surviving deeds, visitations and surveys note that the estate’s documentary trail is ordinary land‑transaction history: the Clegg estates passed through Belfield, Howorth and other families, and the present house is likely a seventeenth‑century rebuild rather than a thirteenth‑ or fourteenth‑century timber manor in which a serial murder took place. The 1889 History of the Parish of Rochdale specifically warns that Roby’s dramatic narrative is “pure imagination” while acknowledging a living tradition of a ghost and even a local proverb, “As ill as Clegg Hall boggart,” meaning hard to get rid of. In short, land deeds and the Manor Survey (1626) document ownership and a substantial house; they do not record the alleged atrocity that underpins the legend. ([your-content.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com](https://your-content.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/04145039/chapter-xvii-old-houses-and-old-families-butterworth-pages337-389.pdf))

How historians and folklorists read that difference matters. Folklore scholars treat the Clegg Hall boggart as a regional example of a wider boggart tradition in Lancashire — mischievous, sometimes malevolent household spirits attached to particular places — and they trace how oral tale, ballad and antiquarian retelling built up the colourful episodes now associated with the site. Local‑history sources, by contrast, look for contemporary legal or parish records to corroborate dramatic claims and find none that support a medieval massacre. Both approaches are valid but answer different questions: one asks how people told and remembered the place, the other asks what can be proved from surviving documents. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25256/25256-h/25256-h.htm))

So does a boggart still haunt Clegg Hall? If you mean “is there corroborated historical evidence of a medieval tragedy that left a ghost,” the answer is no. If you mean “does the story still haunt local memory and appear in collections and ballads?” the answer is yes — the tale is part of Rochdale‑area folklore and was repeatedly collected and retold in the nineteenth century and later. The difference is between living local tradition and verifiable historical fact. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25256/25256-h/25256-h.htm))

If you want to pursue the matter further: the National Heritage List entry is the authoritative source for the building’s architecture and dating; nineteenth‑century folkloric accounts (Roby and others) are the primary sources for the boggart narrative; and county histories and deed records (summarised in the parish history) are the place to check whether documentary evidence exists for any supposed crime. The List entry and county history are the best starting points for anyone who prefers deeds to apparitions. ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

articles.title: Two Rochdale men among ten charged in drugs supply investigation
articles.excerpt: GMP says two Rochdale men are among ten people charged following a seven-month investigation. All ten have been remanded ahead of a Crown Court appearance.
articles.content_html:
Two Rochdale men are among ten people charged following a seven-month investigation into the suspected supply and distribution of drugs across Greater Manchester and the West Midlands.

Greater Manchester Police named the local defendants as Jailil Ahmed, 53, of Twinegate, Rochdale, and Shakil Ahmed, 51, of Whittaker Lane, Rochdale.

In a statement issued on 27 October, the force said eight men, a woman and a 16-year-old boy had been charged with conspiracy to supply controlled drugs in classes A, B and C, and conspiracy to supply an unauthorised medicinal product.

The boy cannot be named for legal reasons. The other adult defendants are from Burnage and Wolverhampton, or have no fixed abode, according to the police statement.

GMP said its Serious and Organised Crime Group carried out the investigation into suspected large-scale supply and distribution in the two regions.

All ten have been remanded in custody ahead of a scheduled appearance at Manchester Crown Court on Friday 13 November 2026, the force said.

The charges are allegations. No finding of guilt should be inferred, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless and until convicted.

articles.title: Middleton prepares for Christmas lights switch-on event
articles.excerpt: Middleton is making final preparations for its Christmas lights switch-on event, scheduled for Saturday, November 14, in Middleton Gardens. The festive atmosphere is already taking shape with decorations appearing throughout the town, including a special red shoe outside Middleton Library in memory of Rochdale Council officer Lauren Mason, who passed away tw
articles.content_html:
Middleton is making final preparations for its Christmas lights switch-on event, scheduled for Saturday, November 14, in Middleton Gardens. The festive atmosphere is already taking shape with decorations appearing throughout the town, including a special red shoe outside Middleton Library in memory of Rochdale Council officer Lauren Mason, who passed away two years ago.

The switch-on event will begin at 12pm and will feature a variety of attractions designed to engage the community and spread festive cheer. Attendees can look forward to food and drink stalls, fairground rides, and market stalls, including the Teenage Market, which supports local young entrepreneurs. Additionally, The Art House will host personalised Christmas card-making sessions and face painting for children.

As the day progresses, visitors will enjoy performances from local community groups, culminating in a performance by Middleton Brass Band at 4.30pm, which will help set the festive mood ahead of the lights being switched on.

This event not only marks the start of the Christmas season in Middleton but also provides an opportunity for local businesses and young entrepreneurs to showcase their offerings. Residents and visitors alike are encouraged to attend and participate in the festivities, making it a significant occasion for the community.

articles.title: Broad Lane roadworks in Rochdale set to begin on 11 January 2027
articles.excerpt: Roadworks on Broad Lane will temporarily close part of the road from January to May 2027, affecting local traffic.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on Broad Lane will commence on 11 January 2027 and are expected to last until 2 May 2027. The works will involve the temporary closure of Broad Lane from the junction with Oldham Road to the junction with Turf Hill Road.

During this period, traffic will be diverted to alternative routes including Oldham Road, Queensway, Kingsway, and Turf Hill Road. Local residents and commuters are advised to plan their journeys accordingly to avoid delays.

The roadworks are part of ongoing improvements aimed at enhancing local infrastructure and ensuring safer travel for all road users. The council has provided a map of the affected area and alternative routes on its website.

Residents are encouraged to check the Rochdale Borough Council's official website for updates on the progress of the roadworks. This development is significant for local traffic management and will impact daily commutes in the area.

articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has received several nominations at the Northwest Football Awards 2026, recognising the club's fan engagement and community initiatives.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has been nominated for several awards at the upcoming Northwest Football Awards 2026, highlighting the club's strong community ties and fan engagement. The awards ceremony will take place on Monday at The Manchester Deansgate Hotel, where finalists from various clubs will gather to celebrate achievements in football.

The club's supporters have earned a nomination for Best Club Fan Engagement, competing against notable clubs such as Carlisle United, Liverpool FC Women, and Salford City. Additionally, Rochdale AFC's Community Trust has been recognised for its Changing Lives FC initiative, which is shortlisted for Community Initiative of the Season alongside other community-focused programmes from clubs like Blackburn Rovers and Bolton Wanderers.

Former Rochdale manager Jimmy McNulty has also been nominated for Manager of the Season following the club's promotion to League Two. He is up against Steven Schumacher of Bolton Wanderers, Pep Guardiola from Manchester City, and Michael Carrick of Manchester United. Furthermore, Rochdale's Sam Beckwith is in the running for the PFA National League Community Champion 2025/26 award, showcasing the club's commitment to community involvement.

Rochdale AFC expressed their delight at being finalists in these categories, stating, “We’re delighted to be named as a finalist at the 2026 Northwest Football Awards.” The recognition not only celebrates the club's achievements but also reinforces the importance of community engagement in football, which resonates with fans and local residents alike.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Rochdale AFC’s fantastic support highlighted among award nominations - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS , SPORT Rochdale AFC’s fantastic support highlighted among award nominations The Dale’s fantastic fans have been recognised among a host of award nominations for the club. On Monday, the finalists will gather for the Northwest Football Awards 2026 at The Manchester Deansgate Hotel. Dale supporters have helped the club earn a Best Club Fan Engagement nomination, alongside Carlisle United Football Club, Liverpool FC Women and Salford City Football Club. The Dale are also in the running for Community Initiative of the Season for Rochdale AFC Community Trust’s Changing Lives FC initiative. Also shortlisted are Blackburn Rovers Community Trust for its Women’s Wellbeing Champions; Bolton Wanderers in the Community’s ASPIRE programme; Fleetwood Town Community Trust-s Go Beyond — Fleetwood Community Hub; and Stockport County Community Trust’s County Pals (Parkinson’s Active Lifestyle Support). Former Dale boss Jimmy McNulty has been shortlisted for Manager of the Season following Rochdale’s promotion to League Two, alongside Steven Schumacher of Bolton Wanderers, former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola, and Michael Carrick at Manchester United. And Rochdale’s Sam Beckwith has been shortlisted in the PFA National League Community Champion 2025/26 category, with Matty Kosylo of Altrincham Football Club, Callum Whelan of Carlisle United, and George Thomas of Morecambe Football Club. Rochdale’s association with the awards continues with the presentation of the Joe Thompson Impact Award, in honour of the Dale legend. Rochdale AFC shared: “We’re delighted to be named as a finalist at the 2026 Northwest Football Awards. READ MORE: Rochdale men among 10 charged with drugs conspiracy Former Rochdale boss Jimmy McNulty has been shortlisted as Manager of the Year. Image: Rochdale Council “Dale have been shortlisted for the Best Club Fan Engagement award, in recognition of the work that has been done to strengthen the relationship between the Club and our supporters. “The establishment of the Club Advisory Board (CAB) has created a valuable platform for supporters to share their views, contribute ideas and help shape the future direction of the club. By encouraging open dialogue and collaboration, the initiative ensures that fans have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting their club. “Alongside this, the Dale 1907 group has played an important role in revitalising the matchday atmosphere, bringing supporters together to generate greater noise, colour, and passion inside the stadium. “Through supporter-led initiatives and a shared commitment to backing the team, the project has helped to strengthen the sense of identity, belonging and collective pride associated with Rochdale AFC. “Together, these initiatives demonstrate a genuine commitment to listening to supporters, empowering fan involvement, and creating a more vibrant, inclusive, and unified matchday experience for the entire Dale family. “Working together, Rochdale AFC and Rochdale AFC Community Trust are committed to bringing fans closer to the club, creating a welcoming, inclusive matchday experience and making sure every supporter feels part of the Dale family. “A huge thank you to our incredible supporters who make this club what it is. This nomination is for you. “Up The Dale! ⚽” SUPPORT THE ROCHDALE TIMES: FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK Got a story? We’d love to hear it! Share your news with us.
